title: ET MALWARE Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Checkin — 10.0.0.11 → 194.36.190.53 (10 check-ins)
description: Internal host 10.0.0.11 is generating repeated Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 check-in connections to the external IP 194.36.190.53 over port 443, with 10 events recorded at consistent roughly 60-second intervals between 01:48 and 01:58 UTC on 28 July 2026. This highly regular beaconing pattern is characteristic of an active Cobalt Strike implant maintaining communication with an attacker-controlled command-and-control server. The ongoing, persistent nature of the check-ins strongly indicates the host is compromised and may be awaiting or already receiving operator commands.
recommended_action: Isolate 10.0.0.11 from the network immediately to cut off the C2 channel, then initiate a full endpoint forensic investigation on that host to identify the Cobalt Strike payload, its persistence mechanism, and any lateral movement or post-exploitation activity that may have already occurred. Additionally, block outbound traffic to 194.36.190.53 at the perimeter firewall and search for any other internal hosts communicating with that IP.

title: ET EXPLOIT Possible Log4j RCE Attempt (Log4Shell) — 91.219.237.244 → 10.0.0.10
description: At 02:00:01 on 07/28/2026, the IDS detected a single inbound TCP connection from external IP 91.219.237.244 (port 51422) to internal host 10.0.0.10 on port 443, matching the Suricata signature for a Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) remote code execution attempt. Log4Shell exploits allow unauthenticated attackers to trigger arbitrary code execution on systems using vulnerable Log4j versions by injecting malicious JNDI lookup strings into logged data. This signature fires on 'Attempted Administrator Privilege Gain' at Priority 1, indicating the payload pattern is consistent with an active exploitation attempt rather than a scan. The timing at 02:00 local time may suggest an automated or targeted off-hours attack.
recommended_action: Immediately isolate 10.0.0.10 from the network if possible, then capture and inspect the full HTTP request payload to confirm the presence of a JNDI injection string and determine whether the server is running a vulnerable Log4j version; also check 10.0.0.10's outbound connections around the same timestamp for any LDAP, RMI, or DNS callbacks to external hosts that would indicate successful exploitation.

title: GPL SQL_INJECTION SELECT FROM — 185.220.101.47 → 10.0.0.20
description: External IP 185.220.101.47 sent 6 SQL injection attempts containing SELECT FROM statements directly to the MySQL port (3306) on internal host 10.0.0.20 over a roughly 44-second window beginning at 02:03:01 on 28 July 2026. The fact that the traffic is hitting port 3306 directly — rather than through a web application layer — suggests the database port may be externally exposed, which significantly increases the severity of this attack. The repeated, evenly-spaced attempts from the same source port indicate a persistent, likely automated exfiltration or enumeration effort.
recommended_action: Immediately verify whether port 3306 on 10.0.0.20 is reachable from the internet and block 185.220.101.47 at the perimeter firewall; then inspect the MySQL logs on 10.0.0.20 for any successful queries, authentication attempts, or data returned to the attacker from that source IP during this timeframe.

title: ET TROJAN Generic Trojan Data Exfiltration Attempt — 10.0.0.20 → 45.155.204.12
description: At 02:09:41 on 28 July 2026, the IDS fired a Priority 1 signature (ET TROJAN Generic Trojan Data Exfiltration Attempt, SID 2027056) on a TCP connection from internal host 10.0.0.20 (ephemeral port 51900) to the external IP 45.155.204.12 over port 8443. Port 8443 is commonly used by malware to blend outbound C2 or data-theft traffic with legitimate HTTPS, making this pattern consistent with a trojan attempting to send stolen data to an attacker-controlled server. The off-hours timing (just after 2 AM) and the nature of the signature elevate concern that this represents active compromise rather than a false positive.
recommended_action: Immediately isolate 10.0.0.20 from the network to prevent further exfiltration, then block 45.155.204.12 at the perimeter firewall and begin forensic triage of the host — reviewing running processes, scheduled tasks, and recent file activity — to identify the trojan and scope any data that may have been exfiltrated.

title: SSH brute-force from 45.155.204.12 — followed by successful login
description: Starting at 03:42:03, source IP 45.155.204.12 conducted a rapid SSH brute-force attack against dc01, generating at least 45 failed login attempts across the 'root' and 'admin' accounts within under a minute. Critically, the alert indicates this campaign was followed by a successful login, meaning the attacker likely gained interactive SSH access to dc01 — a domain controller — using one of these accounts. Unauthorized root or admin access to a domain controller represents a severe compromise with potential for full domain takeover.
recommended_action: Immediately isolate dc01 from the network to prevent lateral movement or further attacker activity, and determine which account ('root' or 'admin') was successfully authenticated, then force a credential reset for all privileged accounts on the host while preserving system logs and active session data for forensic investigation.

title: Port scan detected from 185.220.101.47 against 10.0.0.10
description: External IP 185.220.101.47 conducted a rapid TCP port scan against internal host 10.0.0.10, generating 60 connection attempts within approximately 5 seconds starting at 02:43:26. The scan probed a wide range of destination ports using varying source ports, a pattern consistent with automated scanning tools. All attempts were denied by the firewall (fw01), meaning no connections were established, but the activity indicates active reconnaissance of the internal host.
recommended_action: Investigate 185.220.101.47 using threat intelligence sources (e.g., Shodan, AbuseIPDB) to determine if it is a known Tor exit node, scanner, or malicious actor, and consider adding a permanent block rule on fw01 if confirmed malicious. Additionally, review firewall and IDS logs for 10.0.0.10 to confirm no prior or subsequent successful connections from this source IP or related infrastructure.

title: Repeated connection denials from 172.217.9.201 to 10.0.0.40
description: Between 02:47:16 and 02:48:06 on Jul 28, the external IP 172.217.9.201 made 7 successive TCP connection attempts to internal host 10.0.0.40, all denied by firewall fw01. The destination ports targeted span a range of email-related protocols (SMTP/25, SMTP Submission/587, IMAPS/993, SMTPS/465, IMAP/143, POP3/110) as well as FTP (21), suggesting a systematic probe of mail and file transfer services on this host within under a minute. This pattern of rapid, sequential port scanning against mail infrastructure is consistent with reconnaissance activity.
recommended_action: Investigate whether 172.217.9.201 appears in any threat intelligence feeds or has prior activity in your logs, and confirm that 10.0.0.40 is not inadvertently exposing any of these services externally; if the source IP has no legitimate business justification, consider adding a block rule and escalating if additional activity from this IP is observed.
